briefdescription.para: normal to surface mesh at the Node as based on its connectivity with the surrounding nodes on the surface (cf., computer graphics) TODO: fails for quadrilateral meshes

detaileddescription.para: Computes normal to Node from its neighbor nodes, but ignoring neighbors that are not contained with the supplied Node vector (as in computer graphics) Supplying this vector allows to narrow the calculation to nodes that lie on a line or surface.

The method was created to help check the consistency of the node numbering of lower-dimensional elements representing surfaces prior to converting them into boundaries.
first
iterator to first node in the restricted node range that shall be considered (so that a geometric element can be captured)
last
iterator to last node in the restricted node range that shall be considered (so that a geometric element can be captured)
either the vertex normal or a Point object initialised with signalling NaN
std::find() is used so that the supplied Node range does not have to be sorted (or may consist of 2 sorted ranges, like in a model subdomain)
Explanation of algorithm: for each vertex, calculate the normal of the plane formed by the two edges entering and leaving that vertex. More formally, given vertices 𝐯1,𝐯2,…𝐯𝑛 with counterclockwise winding, define the normal at the 𝑖th vertex as: 𝐧𝑖=(𝐯𝑖−𝐯𝑖−1)×(𝐯𝑖+1−𝐯𝑖)
(where the indices wrap around). The algorithm is implemented using the MJL library in the discretisation/ directory
